To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the added loss in fiber-optics ribbon is caused by axial compressive strain, that this strain is a function of the tape shrinkback and the product αE, and that the added loss for any given environmental cycle can be calculated from this strain.

thermally induced loss is a function of the product αEA, that this product is a function of time and temperature, that the product αEA is the same for all fibers, that this product can be measured by a simple tensile test, and that the product αE can be measured from a single relaxation modulus curve.

the added loss in a fiber ribbon during a temperature cycle is caused by thermally imposed axial compression of the fibers and that the added loss is a function of the product αEA, the tape shrinkback, the time and temperature of the cycle, and the fiber microbending sensitivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of fiber optic cable, the Adhesive-Sandwitch Ribbon (ASR).
the environmental degradation of fiber ribbons and has led to the development of a new type of fiber ribbon, the UA ASR.
the development of a fiber-optic ribbon that will be suitable for use in harsh environments, such as the inside of a jet engine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the added loss for an Adhesive-Sandalwich Ribbon is directly proportional to the product αEA.
the loss of a fiber ribbon is a function of the microbend sensitivity of the fibers and the thermally induced axial strain in the ribbon.
the added loss in a UA ASR is caused by the axial compressive strain that the fibers experience during temperature cycling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a UA ASR with a high δ is required to minimize added loss in a given ribbon.
the environmental performance of UA ASRs can be improved by reducing shrinkback and/or by reducing the αEA product.

the added loss in ASR fibers during temperature cycling is caused by axial compressive strain in the ribboned fiber and that the added loss is a function of δ, the tape shrinkback, and the product αE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss in a UA ASR during temperature cycling is primarily caused by the axial compressive strain induced by the tape shrinkback of the adhesive.
the environmental performance of an ASR with a given δ can be optimized through the choice of the appropriate materials for the coating and tape.
the environmental performance of an ASR with a particular coating is determined by the product αEA, which can be measured using a simple test.
